title: Appendix I: the Prime Material Planes
audit_comment: APPENDIX I: THE PRIME MATERIAL PLANES, printed pp. 117-119, the Alternate Primes doctrine: the universes most familiar, each bordering its own Ethereal with the Astral reaching all - the ways in (the plane shift tuning fork, the amulet of the planes and the well of many worlds, the guarded free-standing gates, the psionic probability travel), and the ways around (no direct Prime-to-Prime spell, the Ethereal-to-inner-to-alternate-Ethereal relay). The Polyverse: an infinite number of Primes, each measured against the traveler's home (0,0,0) by three factors. The physical factor, the level of scientific reality: 1d10 for value, 1d4 odd-negative even-positive for sign, the ladder from +10 (explosive matter, sentience impossible) through the firearms-possible +5, the standard 0, the giant-white-rabbit -3, the aware-chairs -7, to the wholly-aware -10; survival comfortable within 5 either way, home abilities retained abroad. The magical factor, the permeation of magic: from the +10 universal casting that dissolves planes into mage-ruled demi-planes, the +6 visible spells and spell-free saves, the +3 bookless casting, down through the -1 8th-level cap, the -5 Power-spell ban, the -7 where songs disappear, to the -10 where sentient life is impossible - the wizard powerless at -6, the innately magical pooka saving vs. death or dying of deprivation. The temporal factor, the divergence of the planes: +10 the differently colored suns, +6 the methane-breathers, +4 the reshuffled continents, 0 the counterpart individuals of varying alignment, and the negatives the home Prime's own past or future by weeks, years, centuries, millennia, millions of years - the time-travel digression: one's own past unreachable (at least unproven), but the low-negative-timeline alternate the effective equivalent. The general laws: time, gravity, vision and bodily needs the same in all Primes, no general hostility. The class rules: casters limited by the lesser of home and current magical factors; the cleric deity rule (the shared inner, Astral and outer planes against the other-Prime deity's 1st-and-2nd limit); druids and rangers within 2, barbarians within 1, the paladin's mount staying sentient; thieves, fighters, cavaliers, monks normal. The encounters: complete worlds, adapt the tables to the three factors; combat normal at low factors with the high factors arming the unusual and ruining the standard; magic capped by the plane's factor for all casters. And the examples: the same-rules campaign at (0,0,0) with magical drift of 1 or 2 and temporal of at most 5, and the typical 20th-century world at (5,-4,5).

consts.name: ddxPfValueDie
consts.comment: the Prime physical-factor table (the report's box): the factor is chosen by the DM or rolled randomly - 1d10 for the value of the factor, with the printed ladder from +10 (sentience impossible, all matter reacting explosively) through +5 (bipedals over 10 feet unlikely, firearms combustion possible), +3, +1, 0 (the standard: language, animation of inanimates, no size limits on flight or intelligence), -1 (flight by thought, flammables inert), -3 (giant white rabbits), -5 (local gravity, fire without fuel), -7 (aware chairs and trees, humanoid form no longer the norm), to -10 (the entire plane aware, movement by thought, the elements in their pure states, further shifts sending the component parts home).

consts.name: ddxPfSignDie
consts.comment: the sign roll: 1d4 for whether the physical factor is negative or positive - an odd roll negative, an even roll positive; positive factors mean the laws of science hold a firmer grip than home (chemical reactions behave, dragons cannot lift, giants cannot stand), negative factors a lower level of reality (talking animals, self-moving objects, wingless flight, subjective chemistry and gravity).

consts.name: ddxPfComfortRange
consts.comment: the physical survival range: a Prime native is comfortable in alternate Primes within a factor of 5 in either direction on the physical chart - beyond that the world's alien nature is insufficient to maintain the character's life (though beings retain abilities allowed by their home plane's factor even in planes that forbid them: a giant white rabbit survives a +3 plane).

consts.name: ddxDruidPhysRange
consts.comment: the class ranges: druids use their druidical special abilities in planes whose physical factors are within 2 of home, and rangers retain tracking within the same 2 - while barbarians retain their skills only within 1; fighters, cavaliers, monks and thieves function normally.

consts.name: ddxBarbarianPhysRange
consts.comment: the barbarian range: barbarians retain their barbarian skills only in planes whose physical factors are within 1 of that of their home plane - the most homesick of the classes.

consts.name: ddxClericLowSpellCap
consts.comment: the cleric deity rule: the inner, Astral, and outer planes are the same for all alternate Primes, so a cleric whose deity is in an accessible plane regains spells normally - but a cleric whose deity resides in another Prime Material or Ethereal plane can regain only 1st- and 2nd-level spells; undead are turned normally everywhere.

bools.name: ddxPrimesDoctrine
bools.comment: the Primes doctrine: the Prime Material planes are the universes most familiar to players - almost all campaigns begin on one; each plane's inhabitants call theirs the Prime and all others alternate Primes, though in reality all are similar and equally valid, and the majority of the game's rules are designed for them. Reaching them: travelers usually begin in their own Prime; each Prime is bordered on all sides by its own Ethereal plane (so the Ethereal cannot carry you between Primes), but the various Ethereals contact the same single inner planes - Prime to Ethereal to inner plane to alternate Ethereal to alternate Prime - while the Astral reaches all Primes directly; openings to the Astral can be created at any Prime location; no spell takes the caster directly Prime-to-Prime, though some reach eventually via other planes; the plane shift spell moves targets to another Prime with the precise length and material of the required tuning fork known (experimentation often hazardous to the experimenter's life); magical items such as the amulet of the planes or the well of many worlds open ducts between Primes; free-standing gates of unknown origin, often guarded by powerful beings and hidden from common knowledge; and the psionic probability travel renders the traveler physically immaterial for travel to other Primes, entering Ethereal planes to become physically ethereal.

bools.name: ddxPolyverseRule
bools.comment: the Polyverse and the three factors: conceivably an infinite number of Prime Material universes compose an all-encompassing Polyverse whose discovery and cataloguing would defy even the Powers; the differences between alternates are measured by three factors - the physical factor (the level of scientific reality), the magical factor (the degree of magical permeation), and the temporal factor (the closeness of the link to the traveler's Prime); every plane's inhabitants consider themselves the center, and the traveler's home Prime is rated (0,0,0), all others relative to it - a standard AD&D campaign (0,0,0).

bools.name: ddxMagicalFactorRule
bools.comment: the magical factor ladder: the degree to which the plane is permeated by magical energy - the higher the factor the more of the population can cast and the stronger and longer the abilities; the rungs as printed: +10 universal casting among all sentient races, the planes soon dissolving into demi-planes ruled by individuals; +6 all spell effects visible, 11th-level magic possible, no saving throws against magic; +5 10th-level spells, unlimited casts per day; +3 9th-level spells, no spell books or prayers needed, all sentients cast; +1 most sentients cast; 0 the standard with training, study and prayer; -1 8th-level cap, rare casters of one or two races; -3 6th-level cap, clerics only 1st and 2nd; -5 no Power-derived spells, 3rd-level cap; -7 no spells at all, creativity and imagination uncommon, songs disappear; -10 no magic, creativity or imagination - beyond it sentient life impossible.

bools.name: ddxTemporalFactorRule
bools.comment: the temporal factor ladder and the time-travel digression: a high factor means the planes diverged widely in the far past (evolution, continents), a negative factor a close similarity - perhaps the home Prime's own past or future; the rungs: +10 wildly different planetary situation and planar connections (differently colored suns, no atmosphere); +6 alien life (methane-breathing, not carbon-based) in possibly hostile environment; +5 Earth-like with alien-but-familiar types, most life missing; +4 Earth-like with familiar sentients, continents in different patterns; +1 familiar continents and creatures, different society and individuals; 0 similar continents, life and society with counterpart individuals whose actions, attitudes and alignments vary; -1 up to a week in past or future; -3 up to a year; -5 up to a century; -7 up to a millennium; -10 millions of years; and the digression: in the AD&D universe one cannot travel into one's own past (at least unproven), but a traveler can effectively accomplish it by finding an alternate Prime with zeroes for physical and magical factors and a low negative temporal factor.

bools.name: ddxSurvivalRule
bools.comment: the survival doctrine: beings retain the abilities their home plane's physical factor allows even in planes that forbid them; but the magical factor seriously affects the abilities of beings from very different planes - spells and spell-like abilities limited by the plane entered (a high-level wizard powerless in a -6 plane), and an innately very magical being (the printed pooka) brought into a -6 magical factor plane must save vs. death or die of the sudden deprivation; in general physical laws and processes proceed similarly in all Primes - time, gravity, the limits of vision, bodily requirements - with the same high-risk areas (volcanoes, storms, deserts) and no general hostility toward travelers; the most easily reached alternates have low factors, and moving between AD&D campaigns might mean no physical or magical change and a temporal shift of 3 or 4.

bools.name: ddxClassRule
bools.comment: the class rules in alternate Primes: magic-users and illusionists relearn spells limited by the current plane's magical factor, and on moving planes limited by the lesser of the two factors (home and current); clerics under the magical factor with the deity rule (accessible plane - full spells; another Prime's or Ethereal deity - only 1st and 2nd) and normal undead turning; druids within 2 physical factors; thieves, fighters and cavaliers normal; rangers tracking within 2; barbarians within 1; paladins' magical abilities limited by the plane's magical factor, the mount retaining its sentience; monks normal; and the examples - an alternate campaign under the same rules shares the physical factor, varies the magical by 1 or 2 and the temporal by at most 5, while a typical 20th-century world rates (5,-4,5), the magical rating varying with the campaign's nature.

bools.name: ddxEncounterRule
bools.comment: the encounter and combat rules (the report's box): encounters vary from Prime to Prime as these are complete worlds in themselves - adapt the standard encounter tables according to the physical, magical and temporal conditions of each plane; combat functions normally in most alternate Primes, but at higher physical factors the conditions allow unusual weapons while other weapons become useless; and magic in alternate Primes is limited by the plane's magical factor - all spell casting limited regardless of type, abilities that are not restricted usable in full.
